Definition: from G1722 and G1412; to empower:--enable, (increase in) strength(-en), be (make) strong.
BiblicalUsage: To empower, to make strong. Christ enabled Paul and counted him faithful in 1 Timothy 1:12, Paul tells Timothy to be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus in 2 Timothy 2:1, and Saul increased the more in strength after his conversion in Acts 9:22. The call to every believer is the same in Ephesians 6:10: be strong in the Lord, and in the power of His might.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe strength is not something I work up but something I am given — Christ enabled Paul, and He enables me. I hold that the Lord's strength is for His work, not my comfort, and it is always enough for the day's battle.
